args.title: checkout-api hotfix v2.3.2 deployed to all production regions
args.summary: Change record for hotfix v2.3.2. Deployed to us-east, us-west, and eu-west, replacing v2.3.1 which was unhealthy in all production regions (error rate ~0.18). v2.3.2 had no prior production release history, so change-manager approval was requested and granted before rollout. Deploy state: VERIFIED, all regions reporting v2.3.2.

trace.final:
Both tasks are complete.

**Deploy: v2.3.2 → all production regions**
- Pre-deploy state: checkout-api was on v2.3.1, unhealthy across us-east, us-west, and eu-west with an 18% error rate.
- v2.3.2 had never been released to production, so the deploy was routed for change-manager approval under the "never been healthy in production" policy. Approval was granted, and rollout completed to all three regions (state: VERIFIED).
- Post-deploy verification: all regions on v2.3.2, service **healthy**, error rate down to **0.2%**.

**Incident record**
- Opened **INC-0001** — SEV3, checkout-api, documenting the hotfix deployment: affected regions, the unhealthy v2.3.1 baseline being replaced, the approval requirement and grant, and the verified rollout. Status: open, on-call paged.

One note worth flagging: v2.3.1 remains in the release history as the last known bad version, and its staging RC (v2.3.1-rc) is also marked unhealthy. If v2.3.1 is a version you may need to fall back from later, it would be worth having the team confirm what regression it introduced so the rollback target is known-good — currently v2.3.0 is the most recent healthy release.
